title: Reservation hedge & FastPath scaling initiative — Q2 plan
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: This ticket defines the Q2 roadmap for a combined Reservation Hedge program and a new FastPath scaling flow for Dedicated customers. The goal is to reduce failover events caused by reservation shortfalls, improve burst handling for latency-sensitive routes, and provide clearer economic guardrails for customers who opt into variable reservation bands.

Context: Post-2025 growth showed two failure modes when demand spikes: (1) customers hitting their committed reservation ceilings and experiencing denied bursts, and (2) inefficient hedging of reserved vs on-demand inventory leading to higher unit costs. FastPath is a lightweight priority ladder in the routing plane that allows short, latency-prioritized bursts from a small burst-credit pool while Hedge controls reservation rebalancing and short-window overcommit.

This plan bundles product requirements, rollouts, and OKR alignment for the quarter and includes handoffs to engineering, pricing, and support for contract templates and docs.
okrs: Objective: Reduce production burst-deny incidents for Dedicated customers by 60% by end of Q2
KR1: Implement FastPath burst-credit pool and congestion-aware routing on 50% of production traffic (target: 50% routes)
KR2: Deliver Reservation Hedge mechanism with configurable hedging windows (1h, 4h, 24h) and reduce unplanned fallback to hosted by 40%
KR3: Publish customer-facing playbook and run two pilot customers on FastPath + Hedge before end of cycle
milestones: 2026-04-08: Complete API and config schema for FastPath and Hedge (RFC approved)
2026-04-22: Engineering spike complete — prototype FastPath routing & burst-credit accounting
2026-05-06: Beta rollout to 2 pilot customers; collect telemetry and latency/cost deltas
2026-05-20: Revise pricing guardrails and contract language with Sales & Legal
2026-06-10: Wider rollout (canary across 20% of Dedicated routes) and post-launch runbook
success_metrics: burst-deny incidents (P95 routes) down by >=60% vs baseline
average tail latency during bursts improves by >=25% for FastPath-enabled routes
unit cost delta for pilot customers within agreed SLA budget (<= +8% overall)
two signed pilots and one resolved legal pricing clause
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (API & config): expose FastPath boolean + hedging window selector in Dedicated config. Phase 2 (runtime): implement burst-credit pool per customer with TTL and token refill algorithm tuned by historical load. Phase 3 (pilot): enable for opt-in customers, run with telemetry flags, and iterate threshold parameters. Phase 4 (canary): expand to 20% of routes behind feature gates and automated rollback on SLO regressions. Phase 5 (GA): default-off product release with docs, pricing updates, and sales enablement.
acceptance_criteria: API schema merged and client SDKs updated
Burst-credit accounting validated by integration tests and load tests
Pilot customers confirm reduced burst failures in 2-week observation window
Runbook and rollback strategy documented and drilled with SREs
risks_mitigations: Risk: Burst-credit pool could be gamed by noisy tenants — Mitigation: per-route rate limits and anomaly detection; initial pilots opt-in only
Risk: Hedging windows may increase short-term cost — Mitigation: provide conservative defaults and explicit customer opt-in with cost simulation tool
Risk: API complexity for customers — Mitigation: single toggle + presets (conservative, aggressive, experimental) with clear UX and CLI tooling

2026-03-11: Architecture sync with Eng (Liam, Priya) — agreed to implement burst-credit as soft tokens in routing plane; assigned ENG-4120 for prototype
2026-03-12: Legal & Sales pre-brief — Sales asked for example contract language; Legal requested pricing floor before pilot
